subject: Senior Serving Engineer — interview ownership & bar standardization
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Sanchez <emily@talentlink.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Senior Serving Engineer — interview ownership & bar standardization

Hi all,

Putting this thread together to lock down interview ownership and the 'bar' checklist for the Senior Serving Engineer (SSE) loop next week. Recruiting has a candidate (Alex Rivera) with a strong infra background; Emily looped in for scheduling. Before we commit panels, I want to confirm:

- Who will take ownership of system design (latency/cost tradeoffs) vs model-serving-specific questions (KV cache, batching, quantization impacts).
- Who is OK standing as the bar-raiser for scope/leveling and handling debrief anchors.
- Any leveling anchors or red flags we should call out ahead of time (e.g., unknowns around kernel-level optimization vs product-driven tradeoffs).

Attached: ownership_matrix_v1.xlsx, role_scope_onepager.pdf. Also linking the draft debrief rubric in Notion.

Proposed assignment (tentative):
- System design / throughput (ownership): Jonas
- Model-serving internals / inference runtime: Marissa
- Production readiness & rollout policy: Grace
- Bar-raiser (final leveling call): Markus (unless Markus opts out)

Please reply with confirmations, proposed edits to the matrix, and your available interview blocks (Emily — can you dump Alex's availability into this thread once you have it?). Aim to finalize by EOD so we can send prep to the candidate and panel.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Hiring Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Senior Serving Engineer — interview ownership & bar standardization

Rachel — thanks for the clear matrix. Quick thoughts inline and a few asks: 

> Proposed assignment (tentative):
> - System design / throughput (ownership): Jonas
> - Model-serving internals / inference runtime: Marissa
> - Production readiness & rollout policy: Grace
> - Bar-raiser (final leveling call): Markus (unless Markus opts out)

- Confirmed: I'll cover model-serving internals (KV caching, batching heuristics, quantization tradeoffs). I'll explicitly call for quantization experiments and ask candidates for past benchmarks (not just theoretical).
- Suggestion: Add a dedicated signal-handling / incident-recovery question under production readiness — candidate should walk through an incident timeline (detection, mitigation, postmortem). Grace can take that in the rollout/ops chunk.
- Leveling anchors: propose we include two concrete anchors for 'Senior' vs 'Staff' in the rubric: (1) breadth of cross-domain tradeoffs (runtime + infra + product) and (2) ownership: evidence of past decisions that changed unit economics. I'll add language to the rubric.

I attached a short debrief rubric (debrief_rubric.md) with the proposed anchors and a scoring scale (1-5 per pillar). Also added an example red flag: can't explain a significant throughput regression root-cause.

Happy to take the debrief notes if Markus prefers to operate only as the final gate.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Staff ML Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachment: debrief_rubric.md (text/markdown)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Emily Sanchez <emily@talentlink.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Senior Serving Engineer — interview ownership & bar standardization

Thanks Rachel — I can take system design/throughput. A couple of practical notes from scheduling perspective: my best blocks next week are Tue/Wed 10:00-12:00 & Thu 14:00-16:00 PT.

On scope: I'd like to carve the system design slot into two 25-minute sections — first on API-level design (throughput, sharding, fallback policies), second on a micro-optimization case (e.g., KV cache layout and memory pressure). That will help us separate high-level tradeoffs from kernel-adjacent decisions.

Regarding bar-raising: Markus — would you be willing to act as bar-raiser and sign off if the candidate shows clear decision-level ownership and cost/latency tradeoff history? If yes, I'll include a short prompt in my interview notes that maps to the rubric anchors Marissa added.

Emily — candidate has availability Thu afternoon per your last note? If so, let's tentatively hold Thu 14:00-16:00 and I'll split into two panels.

Jonas
Principal Software Engineer
Client-side & Serving

Subject: Re: Senior Serving Engineer — interview ownership & bar standardization

I can serve as bar-raiser for this loop. A few constraints & concrete asks: 

1) Bar-raise checklist (high-level):
   - Evidence of decision-level ownership: can the candidate point to a decision where they traded latency vs cost and owned the trade-off end-to-end?
   - Depth in inference runtime: can they explain KV cache behavior under eviction, and quantify latency impacts of common mitigations?
   - Operational maturity: clear postmortem/alerting story and ability to prioritize remediation under SLA pressure.

2) Logistics: I will not join the first half of Thu afternoon but can join the final 30 minutes for debrief/sign-off (14:45–15:15 PT). If you want me to own the final leveling call, please leave that slot open.

3) Debrief protocol: we should use Marissa's rubric and aim for consensus in the first 15 minutes, then the bar-raiser makes the leveling call if there's a split. I'll capture a short rationale for the sign-off (2–3 bullets).

4) Candidate prep & transparency: Rachel — please include the one-pager scope doc when you send the candidate confirmation (helps set expectations). Emily — any scheduling update? Alex — if you're seeing this, a short note: thanks for your interest, you'll get a quick agenda and links once we finalize availability.

Markus
Director, Inference & Reliability
Redwood Inference
